## Recommended Online Books

The following online books are useful companions to ANTH418. You do not need to read them from beginning to end. Use them as references when you need additional explanation, examples, or guidance with R, statistics, or data visualization.

- [**R for Data Science (2e)**](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/) — Hadley Wickham, Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel, and Garrett Grolemund. A practical guide to importing, transforming, visualizing, and working reproducibly with data in R and the tidyverse.

- [**R and Statistics for Archaeologists**](https://rchaeology.github.io/RchaeoStats/) — An archaeology-oriented introduction to statistical analysis in R, connecting statistical methods with archaeological questions and data.

- [**Modern Statistics with R**](https://www.modernstatisticswithr.com/) — Måns Thulin. An accessible introduction to modern statistical analysis with R, useful for both statistical concepts and their implementation.

- [**Data Visualization: A Practical Introduction**](https://socviz.co/) — Kieran Healy. A clear introduction to principled data visualization using R and ggplot2, especially useful for exploratory data analysis and graphical communication.

- [**ggplot2: Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis (3e)**](https://ggplot2-book.org/) — Hadley Wickham, Danielle Navarro, and Thomas Lin Pedersen. A detailed guide to the grammar of graphics and to building effective visualizations with ggplot2.

## Troubleshooting

[Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd)

Start here when:

- R cannot find a file;
- a package will not load;
- Quarto will not render;
- an object cannot be found;
- your code works in the Console but not when rendering; or
- you are unsure how to interpret an error message.

## Core principle

> **Rendering is the reproducibility test.**

Your analysis should be able to rebuild itself from the code written in the `.qmd` file, without depending on objects left behind in the RStudio Environment.
